items.title: Opening the gym at 5am
items.blurb: Twelve steps from the car park to the first member through the door.
steps: Arrive by 4:45am. Park in the staff bays and check the exterior for anything out of place before you go in.
Disarm the alarm and turn on the entry lights. Prop the front door for now; it closes again at step 10.
Walk the floor with the lights on. Look for equipment left out, spills, and anything broken. Note it in the shift log.
Turn on the reception screens, the music and the class studio displays.
Switch the RECOVER rooms on so the infrared sauna is at temperature for the first booking. Check the ice bath water level and temperature.
Restock towels at reception and in the RECOVER rooms. Check the water station.
Log in to the gym system at reception. Open the day's bookings and the class list.
Check today's class schedule against the coach roster. Message the coach if a class has no cover.
Walk the bathrooms and the change rooms. Restock, and report anything that needs cleaning beyond a wipe-down.
Set the front door to member access at 5:00am sharp. 24/7 members already have fob access; this opens the staffed entrance.
Greet the first members by name where you know it. Ask how their training is going.
Write the opening entry in the shift log: time, anything found, anything reported.

items.title: Closing and lock-up
items.blurb: The staffed day ends; 24/7 access continues. What must be done so the gym runs safely overnight.
steps: Thirty minutes before close, announce that the staffed desk is closing and RECOVER bookings end at the last slot.
Turn the RECOVER rooms off after the last session. Drain and cover the ice bath as per the room card. Leave the sauna door open to air.
Walk the floor. Rack weights, wipe benches, straighten mats. Report anything broken in the shift log.
Restock towels and water for the overnight members.
Close the till, run the end-of-day report in the gym system and file it as the procedure card says.
Check the bathrooms and change rooms one last time.
Set the front door back to fob-only access. Confirm the after-hours signage and the emergency number are visible.
Turn off reception screens and music. Leave the safety lighting on.
Write the closing entry in the shift log, arm the alarm zones that cover the back of house, and leave through the staff door.

items.title: Turning a RECOVER room around between sessions
items.blurb: The ten minutes between bookings, done the same way every time.
steps: Knock and wait for the previous booking to leave. Thank them by name.
Wipe the sauna benches and door handle with the approved cleaner. Replace the bench towel.
Skim the ice bath, check the temperature reading and top up if the level is below the line.
Replace towels, empty the bin, and reset the timer display.
Check the room card: lighting scene, music level, sauna set temperature for the next booking type.
Mark the room as ready in the gym system so the next member can be checked in.
Meet the next booking at reception. Walk them in if it is their first RECOVER session and explain the timer and the call button.

items.title: Handling a Fitness Passport member
items.blurb: What Fitness Passport is, what it covers here, and what it does not.
steps: Fitness Passport is a workplace program. The member's employer pays; they show a Fitness Passport card or the app at the desk.
Every visit is scanned and recorded. No scan, no visit recorded, and ONYX is not paid for it.
It covers gym access and group fitness classes. It does not cover RECOVER sessions, personal training or the Evolt360 scan. Those are paid at the desk like any casual purchase.
If the card or app will not validate, take the member's name and Fitness Passport number, let them train, and log it for the manager to follow up.
A Fitness Passport member who wants RECOVER on a regular basis is a lead for a RECOVER membership. Mention it once, warmly, and leave it there.

items.title: Class check-in and no-shows
items.blurb: Every membership includes unlimited classes. The desk keeps the class list honest.
steps: Open the class in the gym system fifteen minutes before it starts.
Check members in as they arrive. Anyone not booked can join if there is space; add them so the coach's list is right.
Five minutes after the start, mark the unarrived as no-shows.
A member with repeat no-shows gets a friendly word from the coach or manager, not from the desk.
Close the class list once it has started so the numbers reported are what actually trained.

items.title: Incidents and first aid basics
items.blurb: What to do in the first two minutes, and what to write down afterwards.
steps: Stay calm and go to the person. Ask if they are okay and what happened. Do not move someone who has fallen and says they are in pain.
If they are unresponsive, not breathing normally, or bleeding heavily, call 000 first. Then start first aid. The defibrillator location is on the floor plan by reception.
Send another member or staff member to reception to fetch the first aid kit and to meet the ambulance at the door.
For minor injuries, treat from the kit, offer ice, and stay with them until they are comfortable.
Once the person is safe, write the incident report the same day: who, what, where, when, who was present, what was done. Facts only.
Tell the manager on duty before you leave the shift. They decide on any follow-up with the member.
Restock whatever you used from the kit and note it in the shift log.

items.title: Onboarding a new starter with this portal
items.blurb: The portal does the teaching. You do the shadowing and the sign-off.
steps: Before day one, open this portal on the reception tablet and on the starter's own phone. It is one link; nothing to install.
Have them enter their name on first open. The progress card carries it.
Point them at the Week 1 path. The order is deliberate: videos first, the opening shift, then the systems simulations.
Pair each simulation with a shadowed real shift the same week. The simulation teaches the clicks; the shift teaches the people.
At the end of week one, ask for their progress card. Read it against the checklist and sign them off, or agree what week two covers.
Anything the portal got wrong or missing goes to the person maintaining it. It is updated for everyone, not just for the next starter.

items.title: Reading a progress card
items.blurb: What the export from the Me page tells you, and what it does not.
steps: A progress card is a file the starter exports from their own device. It lists every item, its status, the date completed and the simulation score where there is one.
Simulation scores come straight from the simulation player: steps completed, wrong attempts, time taken. A pass is set inside each simulation.
Guides and checklists are self-marked. Treat them as a conversation starter, not proof.
The card is only as complete as the device it came from. Progress does not sync between phones in this version; the person's own phone is their record.
Keep the card with your onboarding notes. When the portal gains a hosted team view, these cards import into it.

items.title: Building the weekly roster
items.blurb: Published Thursday for the week starting Monday. Cover first, preferences second.
steps: Open the roster for the coming week by Wednesday morning. Anything published later than Thursday afternoon is late.
Block the fixed points first: every group fitness class with its coach, and the staffed desk hours at each end of the day.
Fill the opening and closing shifts next. These are the two that cannot be left uncovered, and they need someone signed off on the opening and closing checklists.
Layer in RECOVER cover for the busy blocks: weekday mornings before 9, and weekday evenings after 5.
Now apply leave and availability. Anything requested more than two weeks out is honoured unless it leaves a shift uncovered.
Check nobody is rostered to close then open the next morning. It is legal and it is still a bad shift pattern.
Sanity-check the hours against budget before publishing. Flag to Joey if the week is over.
Publish, then message the team. Swaps go through you, not between staff directly.

items.title: Following up an incident report
items.blurb: The staff member wrote the report. What you do with it in the next 48 hours.
steps: Read the report the same shift it was written. If anything is vague, ask the person while they still remember it.
Call the member within 24 hours. Ask how they are, not whether they intend to complain. Write down what they say.
Photograph anything involved: the equipment, the floor, the spill, the sign that was or was not there.
If equipment was involved, take it out of service with a tag until it has been checked. A tag is cheaper than a second incident.
Decide whether it is reportable. Anything involving an ambulance, a head injury or a member who cannot continue goes to Joey and Katie the same day.
Write your follow-up under the original report: what you found, who you spoke to, what changed.
Close the loop with the staff member. They will handle the next one better if they hear what happened.

items.title: Cancellations, freezes and difficult conversations
items.blurb: Most cancellations are a life change, not a complaint about the gym. Find out which one you are in.
steps: Take the conversation off the desk. A member cancelling in front of a queue will not tell you the real reason.
Ask what has changed. Moving, money, injury, or unhappy with something here. The answer decides everything that follows.
Injury or illness: offer a freeze first. A frozen membership comes back; a cancelled one usually does not.
Money: name the cheaper plan honestly rather than defending the current one.
Unhappy: let them finish, write it down, and say what you will do. Do not discount your way out of a service problem.
Moving or genuinely done: process it cleanly and thank them. A graceful exit is how you get the referral.
Check the terms and conditions for notice and any remaining commitment before you agree to anything.
Log the reason in the gym system. The pattern across a month is worth more than any single conversation.

items.title: Process a freeze and a partial refund
items.blurb: Freeze a membership with an end date, then refund a part month and record the reason against the account.

items.title: What we look at each week
items.blurb: Five numbers, read every Monday. Reference only; the gym system is the source of truth.
body: Five numbers tell you how the week went. Read them every Monday morning before the team arrives.
Visits per active member. The single best predictor of whether someone stays. Under one visit a week across a month and that member is drifting.
Class attendance against capacity. A class under half full twice in a row is a timetable problem, not a coach problem.
RECOVER utilisation by room and by block. Empty weekday middays are normal; empty weekday evenings are not.
New joins against cancellations. The net number matters less than the two lines moving in the same direction.
Cancellation reasons, grouped. Three of the same reason in a month is a thing to fix, not a run of bad luck.

items.title: Membership snapshot, September 2026
items.blurb: The three plans as shown on the site on 17 September 2026. Reference only; the gym system is the source of truth for live prices.
body: Three plans were on the site on 17 September 2026, all with 24/7 access and unlimited group fitness classes, and a $59 joining fee on the direct-debit plans.
ONYX Platinum, 6 months: $34.99 per week, billed fortnightly at $69.98. Marked most popular.
ONYX Black, 12 months: $28.99 per week, billed fortnightly at $57.98. Includes a free Evolt360 body scan and report valued at $50, and a free RECOVER Solo session valued at $45.
ONYX Black, paid in full: $1299 once for 12 months, the equivalent of $24.98 per week. Same inclusions as the 12-month plan.
RECOVER by ONYX is sold separately as monthly memberships and session packages, in Together and Solo rooms.

items.title: Opening Artarmon: what the portal needs
items.blurb: The second site reuses everything here. Five things change.
steps: A second site entry in the portal config: name, address, and which guides differ. Opening and closing will differ; the systems simulations will not.
Fresh captures of any screen in the gym system that differs by site, replaced in the simulation with Replace image. The overlays stay where they are.
The site's own photos for the onboarding videos and the floor tour.
A site switcher on the Me page so a person who works both sites sees the right guides.
The same brand, the same portal, the same progress card. Nothing is rebuilt.

items.title: The monthly scorecard
items.blurb: What to read on the first Monday of the month, and in what order.
body: Read it in this order. The order is the point: members before money, because the money follows.
Active members, and the split between month-to-month and committed terms. A base tilting toward month-to-month is a base that can leave quickly.
Net movement. Joins minus cancellations, plotted across twelve months rather than compared to last month.
Visit frequency across the whole base. This is the leading indicator. It falls a month or two before cancellations rise.
Revenue per active member, including RECOVER, personal training and the Evolt360 scans. A flat membership price with rising revenue per member means the extras are working.
RECOVER utilisation and its share of revenue. The rooms have fixed running costs, so utilisation is the number that decides whether they earn their floor space.
Personal training hours sold, by coach. It is both a revenue line and a read on which coaches members trust.
Cancellation reasons, grouped and ranked. Then pick one to fix this month. One, properly, beats five noted.

items.title: RECOVER: how the rooms earn their space
items.blurb: The commercial case for contrast therapy, in plain terms. Reference only; the accountant has the real numbers.
body: A RECOVER room costs the same whether it runs empty or full: the heat, the water, the space it takes on the floor plan. Everything therefore turns on utilisation.
Two products serve two motivations. Together is social and fills weekends and evenings. Solo is a premium private slot and fills weekday mornings.

The free Solo session bundled into the ONYX Black memberships is an acquisition cost, not a giveaway. It exists so a member experiences the room once; conversion after that first session is what to measure.
Memberships beat casual sessions for a recovery product, because the habit is weekly and a package makes the member plan around it.
The room is also a retention tool for the gym membership itself. A member who books RECOVER weekly has a second reason to keep coming, and second reasons are what stop cancellations.

Watch three things: utilisation by block, the split between Together and Solo, and how many RECOVER members are also gym members. The third one tells you whether the room is growing the business or just moving revenue around inside it.

items.title: Hiring a coach
items.blurb: Qualifications get them in the room. Temperament decides the hire.
steps: Write the role around the gap, not the person. A powerlifting coach and a group fitness coach are different hires with different weeks.
Screen for the non-negotiables on paper: current certification, first aid and CPR, insurance and a working with children check where relevant.
Phone screen for fifteen minutes. You are only checking whether they can hold a warm conversation with a stranger, which is most of the job.
Run a floor trial, paid, during a busy block. Watch whether they approach members unprompted or wait to be approached.
Give them one coaching scenario: a member doing something unsafe who did not ask for help. The way they interrupt tells you how they will treat the floor.
Ask what they do when they do not know the answer. The good answer involves finding out and coming back.
Reference-check the last two employers, and ask specifically whether members asked for that person by name.
Onboard through this portal from day one. Same path, same checklists, same standard as everyone else.

items.title: Keeping this portal current
items.blurb: A portal nobody updates is worse than no portal. Five habits keep it true.
steps: One owner. Somebody's name is against this portal, and everyone knows whose.
Corrections come from the floor. The staff who use it find the errors first, and the Support page tells them where to send them.
When the gym system changes, the screenshots change. Reopen the SimStudio project, use Replace image on the affected steps, export again. The overlays stay where they are.
When a procedure changes, the guide changes the same week. A guide that contradicts the floor teaches the team to ignore the portal.
Review the whole thing quarterly against what actually happens on shift. Delete anything nobody uses; dead content makes the rest look stale.
Roll a new site in by reusing everything. Only the opening and closing guides and the site photos differ.

faq.q: A member's fob or card will not scan.
faq.a: Check the membership is active in the gym system by name. If it is, let them in, note the fob number in the shift log, and reissue at the desk. If it is not active, explain kindly and offer to take a payment or book them in with the manager.

faq.q: Two RECOVER bookings clash for the same room.
faq.a: The system booking wins. Offer the other member the other room type at the same price, or the next free slot with a complimentary extension. Log it so the manager can see how it happened.

faq.q: The Fitness Passport app will not load.
faq.a: Take the member's name and Fitness Passport number, let them train, and log it for the manager to record the visit later.

faq.q: Someone wants to cancel a membership at the desk.
faq.a: Do not process it at the desk. Take their details and the reason, and book them a call with the manager. Cancellations follow the terms and conditions and need the manager's sign-off.

faq.q: Who do I call after hours?
faq.a: The manager on duty for the day is on the shift log. Anything urgent about safety is 000 first, then the manager.
